limitations_and_boundaries: Analysis applies to MPNNs that weigh each edge contribution equally, up to degree normalization; attention/gating mechanisms may alter over-squashing but are not fully analyzed.
Determining when sensitivity is 'too' small depends on readout resolution, which is not considered.
Theorem 5.5 holds in expectation over nonlinearity and encodes average behavior; a more refined exact analysis is left for future work.

research_questions.statement: What is the impact of width, depth, and graph topology on over-squashing in Message Passing Neural Networks?

provenance.text_excerpt: Rayleigh’s monotonicity principle asserts that the total effective resistance decreases when adding new edges – which offer a new interpretation as to why spatial methods help combat over-squashing.

claims.statement: Spatial rewiring methods mitigate over-squashing by reducing effective resistance.

provenance.text_excerpt: The graph topology plays the greatest role, since over-squashing occurs between nodes at high commute time.

claims.statement: Graph topology is the most important factor; over-squashing occurs between nodes with high commute time.

provenance.text_excerpt: Neural network width can mitigate over-squashing, but at the cost of making the whole network more sensitive.

claims.statement: Width can mitigate over-squashing but increases overall network sensitivity.

provenance.text_excerpt: Depth cannot help mitigate over-squashing: increasing the number of layers leads to over-squashing being dominated by vanishing gradients.

claims.statement: Depth cannot mitigate over-squashing; increasing layers leads to vanishing gradients dominating.

provenance.text_excerpt: Theorem 5.5 implies that nodes at small commute time will exchange information better in an MPNN and conversely for those at high commute time.

claims.statement: The symmetric Jacobian obstruction is bounded by commute time, independent of depth.

provenance.text_excerpt: Corollary 5.6 essentially tells us that the obstruction among all pairs of nodes decreases (so better information flow) if the MPNN operates on a graph G with larger Cheeger constant.

claims.statement: Spectral rewiring methods mitigate over-squashing by increasing the Cheeger constant.
